description: Examine major leadership paradigms in organizational psychology, analyzing transformational vs. transactional models, situational leadership, Leader-Member Exchange, and toxic leadership.

slides.title: The Evolution of Leadership Science
slides.content:
# The Science of Organizational Leadership

What makes a great leader? For centuries, folklore assumed leaders were born, not made (**The Great Man Theory**). Over the past 80 years, I-O psychology transformed leadership from myth into rigorous behavioral science:

```
                             [THE EVOLUTION OF LEADERSHIP MODELS]
                                              |
   [1. TRAIT THEORIES (1930s-40s)]    --> What personality traits define a leader? (Intelligence, Extraversion)
                 |
                 v
   [2. BEHAVIORAL STYLES (1950s-60s)] --> What do effective leaders DO? (Task vs Relationship focus)
                 |
                 v
   [3. CONTINGENCY MODELS (1970s-80s)]--> How does the situation dictate the optimal leadership style?
                 |
                 v
   [4. CONTEMPORARY MODELS (1990s+)]  --> Transformational, Authentic, LMX, and Servant Leadership.
```

slides.title: Behavioral Approaches: Ohio State & Michigan Studies
slides.content:
# The Behavioral Revolution: What Leaders Do

In the 1950s, researchers stopped measuring personality traits and began cataloging actual leader behaviors:

## The Ohio State Leadership Studies (Stogdill et al.):
Identified two independent behavioral dimensions:
1. **Initiating Structure (Task-Oriented):** Organizing work, defining roles, establishing schedules, and enforcing deadlines.
2. **Consideration (People-Oriented):** Building mutual trust, respecting subordinates' ideas, and caring for their personal well-being.

## The Michigan Studies (Likert):
- Distinquished **Production-Oriented** from **Employee-Oriented** leadership.
- *Key Finding:* Leaders high in BOTH Consideration and Initiating Structure consistently achieve superior subordinate satisfaction and team productivity!

slides.title: Fiedler's Contingency Model (1967)
slides.content:
# Fred Fiedler: Matching Leader to Situation

Fred Fiedler formulated the first comprehensive **Contingency Model of Leadership**, asserting that leadership effectiveness depends on matching a leader's style to the **situational favorability**:

## The Least Preferred Coworker (LPC) Scale:
- Leaders rate the coworker they least enjoyed working with:
  - **High LPC (Relationship-Oriented):** Rates LPC favorably; values interpersonal harmony.
  - **Low LPC (Task-Oriented):** Rates LPC harshly; values task execution above all.

```
   SITUATIONAL FAVORABILITY (Leader-Member Relations + Task Structure + Position Power)
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   EXTREMELY FAVORABLE SITUATIONS   --> LOW LPC (Task-Oriented) LEADERS EXCEL!
   MODERATELY FAVORABLE SITUATIONS  --> HIGH LPC (Relationship-Oriented) LEADERS EXCEL!
   EXTREMELY UNFAVORABLE SITUATIONS --> LOW LPC (Task-Oriented) LEADERS EXCEL!
```

slides.content: Verify your understanding of Ohio State and Fiedler models!

slides.title: Hersey & Blanchard's Situational Leadership Model (SLT)
slides.content:
# Hersey & Blanchard: Follower Readiness

Paul Hersey and Ken Blanchard proposed that leaders must dynamically alter their leadership style to match the **Developmental Readiness (Maturity)** of their followers:

```
   FOLLOWER READINESS LEVEL               OPTIMAL LEADERSHIP STYLE
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   R1: Low Ability & Low Willingness  --> TELLING (Directing): High Task, Low Relationship.
       (Incompetent and Insecure)         Provides specific instructions and close supervision.
   R2: Low Ability & High Willingness --> SELLING (Coaching): High Task, High Relationship.
       (Motivated but Lacks Skills)       Directs and explains decisions while encouraging.
   R3: High Ability & Low Willingness --> PARTICIPATING (Supporting): Low Task, High Relationship.
       (Capable but Insecure/Hesitant)    Shares decision-making and acts as a facilitator.
   R4: High Ability & High Willingness--> DELEGATING: Low Task, Low Relationship.
       (Expert and Confident)             Turns over complete autonomy and responsibility.
```

slides.title: Transformational vs. Transactional Leadership (Bass)
slides.content:
# The Paradigm Shift: Bernard Bass (1985)

Bernard Bass expanded James MacGregor Burns' work into the dominant framework of modern leadership:

```
                                [THE LEADERSHIP SPECTRUM]
                                            |
         +----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
         |                                                                     |
   [TRANSACTIONAL LEADERSHIP]                                            [TRANSFORMATIONAL LEADERSHIP]
   - Focuses on exchange transactions.                                   - Inspires followers to transcend self-interest
   - Contingent Reward (bonus for output).                                 for the collective good.
   - Management by Exception (Active/Passive:                            - Generates profound paradigm shifts,
     intervening only when errors occur).                                  innovation, and extraordinary performance!
```

Transformational leadership doesn't replace transactional mechanics; it builds upon them to unleash peak potential.

slides.title: The Four I's of Transformational Leadership
slides.content:
# The Anatomy of Transformation: The Four I's

Bass identified four core behavioral dimensions that constitute Transformational Leadership:

```
   1. IDEALIZED INFLUENCE (Charisma)       --> Acts as an impeccable moral role model;
                                               instills pride, respect, and deep trust.
                                               Followers identify passionately with the leader.
   
   2. INSPIRATIONAL MOTIVATION             --> Articulates a compelling, inspiring vision
                                               of the future; challenges followers with high standards.
   
   3. INTELLECTUAL STIMULATION             --> Challenges old assumptions and orthodoxies;
                                               encourages creativity, questions, and novel problem-solving.
   
   4. INDIVIDUALIZED CONSIDERATION         --> Acts as a mentor and coach; attends to each
                                               follower's unique developmental needs and aspirations.
```

slides.title: Leader-Member Exchange (LMX) Theory (George Graen)
slides.content:
# Relational Dyads: Leader-Member Exchange (LMX)

Traditional leadership theories assumed leaders treat all subordinates identically. George Graen and colleagues proved that leaders form **unique, individualized dyadic relationships** with each employee:

```
   [THE LEADER]
        | 
        +-----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
        | (High-Quality Exchange)           | (Low-Quality Exchange)
        v                                   v
   [THE IN-GROUP]                      [THE OUT-GROUP]
   - Mutual trust, respect, autonomy.   - Formal contractual compliance only.
   - High mentoring and plum projects.  - One-way downward directives.
   - Lower turnover, rapid promotion.   - Low satisfaction, high alienation, high turnover.
```

## Modern Leadership Mandate:
Leaders must actively expand their in-groups, offering high-quality developmental exchange to ALL diverse team members.

slides.title: Authentic & Servant Leadership
slides.content:
# Leading with Ethics and Service

Following corporate fraud scandals (Enron, WorldCom), leadership science pivoted toward moral character:

## 1. Authentic Leadership (Avolio & Gardner, 2005):
- **Self-Awareness:** Deep understanding of one's own values, strengths, and blind spots.
- **Relational Transparency:** Open, genuine, non-defensive sharing of thoughts and mistakes.
- **Balanced Processing:** Objectively analyzing all data before making decisions.
- **Internalized Moral Perspective:** Guided by internal ethical standards, resisting social pressure.

## 2. Servant Leadership (Robert Greenleaf, 1977):
- Flips the traditional organizational pyramid upside down!
- The leader's primary goal is not personal power, but **serving the developmental needs of employees and community**.

slides.title: Toxic Leadership & The Dark Triad
slides.content:
# When Leaders Destroy: The Dark Triad

Leadership is not inherently benevolent. High positions of organizational power frequently attract individuals possessing the **Dark Triad** of personality:

```
   NARCISSISM        --> Grandiose entitlement, craving constant adulation, hypersensitive
                         to criticism, exploits subordinates for personal glory.
   MACHIAVELLIANISM  --> Cynical, cold, pragmatic manipulation (*"The ends justify the means"*),
                         adept at political intrigue and deceit.
   PSYCHOPATHY       --> Callous lack of empathy or remorse, impulsive risk-taking, superficial charm.
```

## Abusive Supervision (Tepper, 2000):
Sustained hostile verbal and nonverbal behavior (ridiculing subordinates, silent treatment) inflicts severe allostatic stress, triggering anxiety, absenteeism, and organizational sabotage.

slides.title: Gender and Leadership: The Double Bind
slides.content:
# Breaking the Labyrinth: Gender & Leadership

Despite women earning over 50% of advanced degrees, they hold under 10% of Fortune 500 CEO roles (Eagly & Carli, *Through the Labyrinth*).

## The Leadership Double Bind (Role Congruity Theory - Alice Eagly):
- Society's mental prototype of a "Leader" is agentic (assertive, dominant, tough).
- Society's mental prototype of a "Woman" is communal (warm, nurturing, caring).

```
   Agentic Female Leader  --> Judged as "abrasive, aggressive, unlikable, and harsh!"
   Communal Female Leader --> Judged as "too sweet, weak, indecisive, and lacking executive presence!"
   ==> A NO-WIN COGNITIVE CATCH-22!
```

Meta-analyses prove that female leaders systematically score higher on **Transformational Leadership** dimensions than male peers!

slides.title: Cross-Cultural Leadership: The GLOBE Project
slides.content:
# Global Leadership: Robert House et al. (2004)

The **GLOBE Study** examined 17,300 managers across 62 societies to identify universally endorsed versus culturally contingent leadership attributes:

```
   UNIVERSALLY DESIRABLE LEADERSHIP ATTRIBUTES   CULTURALLY CONTINGENT ATTRIBUTES
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   - High Integrity and Honesty                 - Individual Autonomy / Independence
   - Inspirational Vision and Charisma          - Participative / Egalitarian Decision-Making
   - Decisiveness and Team-Orientation          - Status-Consciousness and Formal Protocol
   - Foresight and Strategic Planning           - Paternalism (protective father figure)
```

Participative leadership is celebrated in egalitarian Scandinavia, but viewed as weak and incompetent in high-Power-Distance hierarchical cultures.

slides.title: Leadership Development: 360-Degree Feedback & Coaching
slides.content:
# Cultivating Leaders: Modern Development Methods

How do organizations develop transformational leaders?

## 1. 360-Degree Multi-Source Feedback:
- Performance ratings collected simultaneously from:
  - Superiors (boss)
  - Direct Subordinates
  - Lateral Peers
  - The Leader Themselves (Self-Evaluation).
- Dismantles executive blind spots by highlighting discrepancies between self-image and peer perception.

## 2. Executive Coaching & Stretch Assignments:
- Placing developing leaders in ambiguous, high-stakes international assignments (*"crucible experiences"*) accelerates emotional self-regulation and strategic adaptability.

slides.title: Shared & Distributed Leadership
slides.content:
# Beyond the Heroic CEO: Shared Leadership

In complex, knowledge-intensive industries, the myth of the solitary heroic leader is collapsing:

## What is Shared Leadership?
An emergent team property wherein leadership roles and influence are dynamically distributed among multiple team members based on domain expertise rather than formal hierarchy.

```
   Stage 1: Technical Architecture Problem --> Senior Engineer takes leadership.
   Stage 2: Client Contract Negotiation   --> Account Executive takes leadership.
   Stage 3: Team Conflict De-escalation    --> Empathetic Project Manager takes leadership.
```

Teams practicing shared leadership exhibit significantly higher agility, innovation, and resilience.

slides.title: Comparative Analysis of Leadership Paradigms
slides.content:
# Theoretical Comparison of Leadership Paradigms

| Leadership Paradigm | Primary Focus | Core Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **Contingency Model (Fiedler)** | Leader-Situation Fit | LPC match to situational favorability. |
| **Situational (Hersey & Blanchard)**| Follower Readiness | Telling, Selling, Participating, Delegating. |
| **Transformational (Bass)** | Vision & Inspiration | 4 I's transcend subordinate self-interest. |
| **Leader-Member Exchange (LMX)** | Dyadic Relationships | In-group trust vs Out-group contract. |
| **Authentic Leadership (Avolio)** | Moral Transparency | Self-awareness, ethics, balanced processing. |
| **Servant Leadership (Greenleaf)** | Altruistic Service | Prioritizing employee growth above power. |

slides.title: Module Synthesis: Leadership Theories
slides.content:
# Key Takeaways: Leadership Theories

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                 MODULE SUMMARY MATRIX                                   |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| Theory / Model        | Key Pioneers                | Core Leadership Principle         |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| Ohio State Studies    | Stogdill (1950s)            | Initiating Structure (Task) and   |
|                       |                             | Consideration (People) behaviors. |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| Transformational      | Bernard Bass (1985)         | 4 I's: Idealized Influence,       |
| Leadership            |                             | Inspiration, Intellect, Attention.|
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| LMX Theory            | George Graen (1975, 1995)   | Individual dyadic relationships:  |
|                       |                             | In-group trust vs Out-group rules.|
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| Role Congruity Theory | Alice Eagly (2002)          | Prejudices create double binds    |
|                       |                             | for agentic female executives.    |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
```

## Final Lesson:
True leadership is not an authoritarian exercise of power, but the capacity to inspire vision, nurture diverse talent, cultivate ethical trust, and build adaptive human teams.
